![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095768/assets/db042c1d6bc23ed95988fe1a83a565065928dca06ffe454225da6c638a70f741.png)

Consider the shaded region $D$ shown above. What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\pi \cdot {3}^{2}=9\pi .
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=4\cdot (-2)-(-3)\cdot 2=-2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|-2|\cdot 9\pi  \\  & =18\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Area Scale Factors of Linear Transformations
